text:
B: Hello. Can you hear me alright?
A: Er, yeah. Yeah, fine.
B: Good. I'm Imran, I'm in Huddersfield.
A: Gareth. Wrexham.
B: Wrexham. I've never been, I'm afraid. What do you do, Gareth?
A: Erm, admin. Transport office at a building supplies place. Deliveries, dispatch spreadsheet. That sort of thing.
B: Oh, spreadsheets. Do you build them yourself, or is it one somebody set up?
A: Someone else did it, years back. I just sort of filter it and copy the formulas down, you know.
B: That's most people, honestly. I'm in IT support, part-time, so I see a lot of spreadsheets that one person built in 2009 and nobody dares touch.
A: Ha. Yeah, that's ours. If it breaks, I dunno what we'd do, really.
B: Well, sorry, this is a bit of a work habit, but is it backed up anywhere? Because if it's sat on one person's desktop and that machine goes, that's it, it's gone. I'd honestly get your manager to put a copy on the shared drive, or OneDrive if you've got Microsoft 365. Takes five minutes, and it saves a very bad week, if that makes sense.
A: Erm. Don't actually know. I'll have a look.
B: Is that alright? I didn't mean to lecture you.
A: Nah, it's fine. Fair enough, that.
B: What do you do outside work?
A: Football. Wrexham. Bit of PlayStation. Walk the dog.
B: Is that a Staffy bed I saw?
A: Yeah. Dot. She's alright. Chewed the telly remote cable last week.
B: Oh dear. Did you sort it?
A: Taped it up. Works, mostly. I'm alright with that sort of thing. Wi-Fi and that, the PlayStation.
B: Then you're more technical than half my clients. The dentist rang me last month because the printer was "broken". It was switched off at the wall.
A: Ha. Yeah.
B: Do you go to the Wrexham games, then?
A: Few times a season. With my dad, usually. Or my brother-in-law.
B: That's nice, going with your dad. I take my son to Headingley for the cricket now and then. My dad used to take me, years ago.
A: Yeah. Erm, my dad had a heart scare last year, so I sort of go round more now. And the football's a thing we do, you know.
B: I'm sorry to hear that. My dad's got a heart condition too. He's seventy-nine. I cut my hours down partly so I could take him to his appointments.
A: Right. He alright?
B: Mostly, yes. Good days and bad days. Yours?
A: Yeah, he's fine now. Tablets and that. Mum's got him walking.
B: That's the best thing, walking. I'm up Castle Hill most days.
A: I just do round the block with Dot.
B: That still counts, you know. Every step counts, my son keeps telling me. Mostly because he's bored of me talking about my step count.
A: Ha. How many do you do?
B: Twelve thousand on a good day. Not on Wednesdays, though, because the kids come round for tea and I'm...
